top_fixes.rule: Same table as R33 (listed as the overridden target of memo item 5); see R33 for every row. HARD applies for hardship-declined-transfer until 14 October 2026.
top_fixes.why: Today is 10 Oct 2026, before the memo's 14 Oct switch, so every hardship-declined-transfer case expects close_call no_promise/HARD but fin_hardship always sends HSHP (also fails R51).
top_fixes.fix: fin_hardship code: replace vars['reason'] = 'HSHP' with vars['reason'] = 'HARD' if vars['today_iso'] < '2026-10-14' else 'HSHP' (keep outcome 'no_promise'); add HARD to the close_call tool reason enum/description and to the FINS/finalize() hardship mapping used by the multi-product close.

top_fixes.rule: From 14 October the third attempt ("final-offer repeat") is withdrawn: attempt 1 (F and S) amount in play on the next business day; attempt 2 (S only) the floor on the latest date. Never repeat an offer that has been turned down.
top_fixes.why: a1 = next_bd(today) resolves to today on any business-day call, so attempt 1 re-offers the already refused 'today' date (skipped as refused), collapsing the ladder to a single floor offer and breaking 'never repeat a turned-down offer' (also fails R67 one-by-one flow).
top_fixes.fix: prepare code: change a1 = next_bd(today) to a1 = addbd(today, 1) (next business day strictly after the call date) wherever the attempt-1 / start_product rung-0 date is computed, so attempt 1 is 'amount in play on {{a1}}' and attempt 2 the floor on the latest date, and the per-product ladder never asks about today again.

top_fixes.rule: "Next <weekday>" is the first such weekday after the call date even in the same week; "this <weekday>" or a bare weekday is the same day; if the call is on that weekday, "this" means today and "next" means seven days later.
top_fixes.why: resolve_when turns 'next Friday' into +7 beyond the first Friday and bare/'this' Friday on a Friday into +7 instead of today, so read-back and create_promise dates are wrong in every weekday case.
top_fixes.fix: check_offer code resolve_when: delta = (wd - today.weekday()) % 7; if delta == 0: delta = 0 if qualifier in ('this', None) else 7; else: use delta for both 'next X' and 'this X'/bare X; remove the weekday_table_first_after_plus7 '+7' rule in setup.

top_fixes.rule: One named date for everything is checked per product: a product whose latest date is earlier goes on its own latest date (said in the read-back); a closure day is moved per 4.6 for each product; others keep the named date.
top_fixes.why: fit_day moves a named Saturday/Sunday/closure day to next_bd while 4.6 and the spoken read-back say 'the nearest business day before the day you named', so multi-product closure-day cases get the wrong date (also fails R95).
top_fixes.fix: prepare code fit_day: replace dd = next_bd(dd) with nb = prev_bd(dd); dd = nb if nb >= today else next_bd(dd), mirroring check_one's closed_day_move == 'before' branch, so the 'bd' tag read-back and the proposed date agree.

top_fixes.rule: For a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when I get paid"): ask once for the exact day; if none, propose the last business day of the current week (if the call is on it, the next business day after); if after the latest date, propose the latest date.
top_fixes.why: After the one 'Which exact day would that be?' ask, the vague branch always proposes the product's latest date instead of the last business day of the current week, so 'next week / when I get paid' cases get the wrong proposed date.
top_fixes.fix: check_offer code check_one vague branch: compute wk = lastbd_of_week(today); if today == wk: wk = addbd(today, 1); prop = wk if wk <= dl else dl; then set_prop(V, pid, pa, prop) and say T('vague_deadline', deadline=txt_short(prop), ...) instead of dl.
